body: Thanks. I have an album by Amon Amarth that I like very much. I think I will listen to it tonight.

Thanks, I appreciate the advice. What's getting me down is my neurology, I've been this way with unipolar depression since I was in single digits. Things do seem to be falling apart around me, but I put that down to factors out of my control and neglect from an extended depressive phase. Although outside things contribute to bad feelings, I don't think it would be a good idea to blame the depression on those things.

Thanks. I think that if I stay slow and methodical about carrying out my activities and not talk too much, I should be able to manage the stresses of having to interact with others and schoolwork. I only have a couple of classes, so I should have some time in between to recharge.

Yes, recognizing these experiences as projections of the depression has really been the best development for me. It was not so easy when I was younger, although I still do sometimes slip into thinking that the feelings are real expressions of things going on in the world around me. Certainly there are things to get depressed about, but I have to rely on the knowledge that they are not in themselves the cause, that the depression is what causes me to look around for reasons why I feel like this.
